CHIEF COMPLAINT
Consultation for breast reduction

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 25-year-old female presenting for evaluation of breast reduction surgery. She has been considering this procedure for approximately 6 to 7 years. She reports back pain and neck pain that have been present since high school, with symptoms worsening when working at her desk for extended periods. She has been attending a chiropractor for several years. She experiences bra strap indentations on her shoulders. She occasionally has numbness or tingling in her hands and sometimes experiences nipple pain. Her breasts are always sweaty but she denies rashes underneath them. She reports that her breast size limits certain activities including working out, jumping, and running due to pain. She currently wears a 34 E sports bra. She has no children at this time but may plan to have children in the future. She has lost 10 pounds over the past few months and would like to lose an additional 20 pounds. This is her first consultation regarding breast reduction.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for: Back pain, neck and upper back pain, bra strap indentations, occasional numbness and tingling in hands, occasional nipple pain, persistent breast sweating, activity limitations related to breast size.
Negative for: Rashes underneath breasts.
Constitutional: Lost 10 pounds over past few months, would like to lose 20 more.
Social: Occasional wine consumption.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Migraines

MEDICATIONS
Propranolol for migraine management

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at age 40. Patient counseled that recommendation is to start mammograms at age 30.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Occasional wine consumption. Currently a student studying psychology. Works at a desk. Married.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Breasts: Inspection reveals asymmetrical breasts with severe bilateral ptosis. One breast is lower than the other. No nipple retraction or discharge bilaterally. No breast tenderness, masses, or axillary lymphadenopathy palpable. Measurements obtained.

RESULTS
Body Surface Area (BSA): 2.65. Schnur scale minimum required resection: 1,792 grams (attainable). Potential for nipple graft given extent of reduction required.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia presenting for breast reduction consultation. She is an ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty. She has attempted nonsurgical management with minimal relief.

Plan:
1. Clinical photographs to be obtained today
2. Document patient symptoms for insurance submission
3. Will submit for insurance approval once patient's insurance changes (expected July)
4. Surgical procedure to include: Anchor-pattern incision around nipple, resection of excess breast tissue and fat, nipple repositioning and elevation to address back and neck pain. Estimated operative time approximately 3 hours. Bilateral drains to be placed for approximately 1 week. One-night hospital stay for postoperative monitoring.
5. Counsel regarding postoperative expectations: Bruising expected and will resolve; nipple sensation typically preserved but small risk of alteration or loss; approximately 30% of patients experience breastfeeding difficulty postoperatively; breasts may change with weight gain and pregnancy.
6. Activity restrictions postoperatively: No heavy lifting for 6 weeks; no driving for 2 to 3 weeks.
7. Patient to notify office when new insurance information becomes available.
8. Follow-up appointment to be scheduled prior to surgery for final review of instructions and questions.
